description: National Liquefaction Loss Database is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Alexander Chansky, Tufts University (tufts.edu). This dataset consists of estimated liquefaction losses associated with historical US events from 1964 - 2019. While many papers and datasets exist regarding the damage caused by individual liquefaction events, liquefaction loss data is rarely aggregated and presented to the public for future loss estimating purposes. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-exeg-dy75. Keywords: Liquefaction, Loss, Earthquake, Hazard. Published 2022-08-05. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
